questions.q: How does this lesson define blast radius?
options: The likelihood that a given credential will be compromised
The cost of a cyber insurance policy
The total number of users in an organization
The maximum scope of damage possible if one specific credential or resource is compromised, regardless of how likely that is
questions.explain: Blast radius is a structural fact about what a compromised credential or resource could do, separate from any estimate of how likely compromise is.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say blast radius is more useful to pin down than a likelihood estimate?
options: Likelihood estimates are always required by regulators, so they aren't useful for internal reviews
Blast radius is cheaper to calculate using automated tools
Likelihood estimates are routinely revised downward and are easy to argue about, while blast radius is a structural fact a review can verify directly
Likelihood and blast radius always produce the same number
questions.explain: Likelihood estimates get argued over and revised; blast radius depends on structural facts like IAM scope and network reach that a review can check directly.

questions.q: Which three dimensions does the lesson say must be traced separately to estimate blast radius?
options: Budget, headcount, and compliance status
Identity reach, network reach, and detection time
Patch level, antivirus status, and firewall rules
Cloud provider, region, and uptime SLA
questions.explain: Identity reach (actual IAM/RBAC permissions), network reach (what a compromised device can connect to), and detection time (how long abnormal use would go unnoticed) don't move together and each must be traced on its own.

questions.q: Why do golden images and shared VM templates commonly grow blast radius according to this lesson?
options: They often carry the same embedded credentials or agents into every instance built from them, so compromising one instance can expose the credential material for all of them
They require more expensive licensing than custom images
They are automatically given domain admin rights by default
They cannot be updated once deployed
questions.explain: A shared base image's baked-in credentials or service principal gets reused across every instance, so compromising one instance can compromise the shared credential material for many.

questions.q: What makes a blast-radius estimate useful to an architecture review, according to this lesson?
options: It is reasoned about verbally once and then discussed informally without being recorded
It only needs to be produced after an incident occurs
It is written down as a documented artifact attached to the design, answering what a credential or resource can actually reach and how abnormal use would be detected
It is calculated exclusively by the compliance team, separate from engineering
questions.explain: A blast-radius estimate only does its job if it is documented and attached to the design so the review can catch an over-scoped credential or undetectable abnormal use before deployment.
